name: Saint John I
history: A pope sent against his will by Theodoric, the Arian Gothic king of Italy, to plead with the Emperor in Constantinople on behalf of the Arians. He was the first pope to visit Constantinople and was received with great honour. When he returned, Theodoric had him imprisoned at Ravenna, where he died. He is honoured as a martyr.
life: John was a Tuscan, an elderly deacon of the Roman Church when he was elected pope in 523. Italy was ruled by Theodoric, king of the Ostrogoths, an Arian Christian who had governed tolerantly for many years but grew suspicious as he aged; he had the philosopher Boethius put to death around this time. When the Emperor Justin I began to take churches from the Arians in the East, Theodoric forced the pope to lead an embassy to Constantinople to have the measures reversed. John was greeted there by the Emperor and the people, and celebrated Easter in Hagia Sophia in the Latin rite. The mission was only partly successful, and on his return Theodoric held him at Ravenna, where he died in May 526, worn out by his treatment. His body was carried to Rome and buried in Saint Peter’s.
prayerTo: Saint John, you were sent on an impossible errand and suffered for refusing to betray your flock. Pray for the Pope, for Christians who live under hostile powers, and for unity between East and West. When I am placed in a hard position, help me to act with honesty and trust in God. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the unity of Christians of East and West, and for anyone you know who is caught between conflicting loyalties.
meditation: He was asked to do what he could not in conscience fully do, and he went anyway, as far as he could go. Where must you obey without compromising the truth?
